title: Feature-edge detection and cross-field alignment to creases
description:
First half of 'feature aligned patches for the quad layout'. Add a `select_feature_edges` node producing a per-edge BoolField (dihedral angle above `angle_degrees`, optional min chain length) in the same shape mark_edges/EdgeMarks already use, and a SharpEdgeConstraint ConstraintSource next to CurvatureConstraints so the cross field is pinned parallel to selected edges (KCP*13 alignment constraints; LCK21a section on feature constraints). The cross-field node gains an optional `feature_edges` BOOLEAN input. Feature edges then flow downstream as a BoolField selection (standing ruling: cone points and feature edges are their own values, never sub-components of a UV field). PATCH-89 (Lyon section 4.4 feature lines and boundary alignment in the motorcycle graph) is the downstream half -- forcing layout arcs onto the feature curves -- and is blocked by this ticket; do not re-create it under CRAW.

SCOPE CORRECTION (user, 2026-09-05): feature edges must be DISCOVERED from the mesh's curvature, automatically inside the pipeline, not authored by wiring a node with a dihedral threshold. The first pass built select_feature_edges (per-edge BoolField, dihedral angle) and a feature_edges input on cross_field; keep both as the reusable node and override port, but: (a) the node's default source becomes curvature-based crest lines -- reuse CrestLineDetector's extremum-along-eigenvector test and polyline tracing (geometry/mesh/data, Yoshizawa 2005) but drive it from the multi-radius Cohen-Steiner integrated curvature tensor already computed by CurvatureConstraints (BZK09 section 3, geodesic disks from target_edge_length out to 10x, contrast-gated), NOT from the 1-ring PrincipalDirectionField, which fragments on dense noisy scans; keep the dihedral test as a second source for CAD-like creases; expose one sensitivity input rather than per-mesh thresholds; (b) quad_layout / cross_field run that same detector automatically when no feature_edges input is wired, sharing the tensor computation with CurvatureConstraints rather than walking the mesh twice; (c) verification must include a smooth mesh (fertility and rocker-arm), where discovered ridge/valley lines must be visible in the cross-field examination overlay with zero DSL wiring, in addition to the beveled cube. Related: PATCH-11 (crest-line failure modes), PATCH-99 (CIE*16 scale invariance), PATCH-100 (full multi-radius shape operator), PATCH-89 (arcs along feature lines, downstream).
definition-of-done:
1. `select_feature_edges` node registered, documented in socketDocs, catalog regenerated. 2. `cross_field` accepts feature_edges and the resulting field is parallel to every selected edge within 2 degrees on a beveled-cube fixture. 3. CrossFieldExaminationScene shows selected edges via setFeatureEdgeOverlay and the aligned field. 4. Unit test on the beveled-cube fixture asserts alignment; no mesh files in the unit suite. 5. Fertility baseline unchanged when no feature edges are supplied. 6. Build checkstyle-green.

7. select_feature_edges defaults to curvature-discovered crest lines built on the integrated curvature tensor; the dihedral source is optional. 8. quad_layout and cross_field discover feature edges automatically when feature_edges is not wired (a public boolean disables it); the beveled cube's 12 creases are still found with no DSL wiring. 9. On fertility and rocker-arm the discovered feature lines are non-empty, form connected polylines along visible ridges/valleys (screenshot), and the fertility baseline (13853 quads, 284 patches, 44 singularities, euler -6) is reproduced when auto-discovery is disabled; counts with it enabled are recorded. 10. The tensor is computed once per pipeline run and shared between the detector and CurvatureConstraints (benchmark shows no second full-mesh walk).
testing-plan: 1. Unit: beveled cube (GridMeshNode-built) -> select_feature_edges at 30 degrees selects exactly the 12 crease chains. 2. Unit: cross field with those constraints has per-face direction within 2 degrees of the adjacent crease. 3. run-scene cross-field scene on a decimation-free crawfish scan (once CRAW-2 lands) or on rockerarm; screenshot shows arcs of the field following ridges. 4. Regression: quad-layout scene on fertility reproduces the baseline counts.
todos: Implement select_feature_edges (dihedral threshold, chain filter) returning a per-edge BoolField
Implement SharpEdgeConstraint as a ConstraintSource and wire into CrossField assembly
Add feature_edges input port to the cross_field node and QuadLayoutEngine.build path
unknowns: Hard vs soft constraints: KCP*13 alignment is soft; whether creases should be hard-pinned like boundary edges
How feature edges interact with the gauge anchor and existing boundary constraints on open meshes
Which radius of the multi-radius series (or which contrast rule) selects crest lines best on scans; PATCH-100's windowed validity may be needed
Whether auto-discovered feature lines should feed only the cross field (this ticket) or also become arcs immediately (that is PATCH-89)
changes-made: Added select_feature_edges node (nodes/selection/SelectFeatureEdgesNode.java): per-edge BoolField of interior edges whose dihedral angle exceeds angle_degrees, minus crease chains shorter than min_chain_length; active-edge order, the mark_edges/EdgeMarks shape. Registered, socketDocs complete, catalog regenerated (108 -> 109 nodes).

Added SharpEdgeConstraints next to CurvatureConstraints: marks the supplied creases as CrossField.alignmentEdges (KCP*13 section 5 soft alignment load) and pins both incident faces under ConstraintSource.FEATURE for the constraint overlay; counts selected edges, pinned faces and conflicts.

cross_field and quad_layout gained an optional feature_edges BOOLEAN input (NDirectionField.FEATURE_EDGES; the existing output port is now FEATURE_EDGES_OUT on the same wire name). When a selection is supplied, detectAlignmentEdges uses boundary edges plus that selection and skips dihedral detection; null keeps the pre-CRAW-5 path byte-for-byte.

New beveled_cube.dsl fixture graph (primitives only, no mesh file): 2-unit cube, 45-degree chamfer 0.25, corner triangles, one octant mirrored across X/Y/Z, then select_feature_edges at 30 degrees with min_chain_length=2 and cross_field fed that selection. Welds to V=302 E=900 F=600, closed genus 0.

Two unit tests in FeatureEdgeAlignmentTest: selection keeps 144 crease edges (24 square-to-bevel lines x 6 segments) and drops the 24 corner-triangle single-edge chains (168 before the chain filter); the field is parallel to the creases within 0.475 degrees on the 96 cone-regular crease edges and 3.849 degrees on the 48 that touch a crease junction.

CrossFieldExaminationScene registers the fixture as the beveled-cube graph, overrides loadGraph, and shows the crease selection through setFeatureEdgeOverlay (STAGES shader mode) alongside the cross and constraint glyphs on both the file and graph paths. Screenshot at tmp/craw-5-beveled-cube-aligned-field.png in the craw-5 worktree.

launch.json entry 'CRAW-5: Cross Field (beveled cube, feature aligned)' launches ixdar.canvas.IxdarWindow with args cross-field-exam and -Dixdar.model=graph:beveled-cube. The graph display name is space-free because the VS Code Java launcher joins vmArgs entries with spaces.

Fertility regression reproduced exactly with no feature edges supplied: 13853 quads, 284 patches, 44 singularities, euler -6. Build and checkstyle green; FeatureEdgeAlignmentTest, MeshNodeRegistryTest and QuadLayoutNodeChainTest all pass.

NOT DONE: definition-of-done item 2 asks for 2 degrees on every selected edge; met (0.475 deg) on the 96 cone-regular creases but not on the 48 touching a crease junction (3.849 deg). At a junction the incident angles sum to 330 degrees, so KCP*13's per-vertex rescaled frame stretches the two perpendicular creases' 90 degrees to 98.18 and the best cross splits the excess: 3.75 degrees Euclidean, irreducible for any vertex-based field. Invariant under mesh refinement and under featureAlignmentWeight (swept 1..1024: 3.799-3.849 deg). Closing it needs a doubly-chamfered corner in the fixture so each crease terminates at its own vertex. See VERIFICATION.md.

PASS 2 (scope correction): feature edges are now DISCOVERED from curvature automatically. CurvatureFeatureDetector (quadlayout/crossfield/constraint) traces ridge/valley lines of the multi-radius Cohen-Steiner integrated tensor and unions them with the dihedral test, emitting the same per-edge BoolField in active-edge order.

CurvatureConstraints split into buildAdjacencyCaches() + computeFaceCurvature(maximumRadius) (one cached integration pass, results in the new FaceCurvatureSamples) + applyCurvatureConstraints() (pinning only, reading the cache). Second constructor CurvatureConstraints(mesh) samples with no field to pin. Hardened for open meshes: the adjacency build called halfEdgeEndVertex on boundary half-edges (next = -1) and crashed on any mesh with a boundary.

CrestLineDetector refactored to run off any VertexCurvatureSource (new interface; PrincipalDirectionField implements it) with CrestDetectionSettings; nested CrestLines promoted to a top-level class. Two tracing bugs fixed: the backward walk re-oriented against its own previous step (so it turned around after one step) and the seed was marked visited only after both walks. On the sine-ridge fixture that is the difference between 60 stubs of <=3 points and 4 polylines of 31 points. SemanticPatchDecomposer/PatchDecomposerCLI unchanged apart from the rename.

MeshVertexCurvature carries the face tensors to vertices (area-weighted into the vertex tangent plane, re-diagonalized). Note the Cohen-Steiner swap: the tensor's eigenvalue along a direction is the principal curvature perpendicular to it, so kappaMax pairs with the OTHER eigenvector; the cross-field pin never cared (quarter-turn symmetry) but crest tracing does.

select_feature_edges now defaults to the curvature crest lines (use_curvature, default true) with use_dihedral (default true) as the second CAD source; one sensitivity input (0..1, default 0.5) replaces the per-mesh thresholds, scaling the crest median-curvature multiple, the umbilical gate, the geodesic-disk radius (9x average edge at 0.5, capped at 0.15 x bounding-sphere radius) and the dihedral threshold (40 degrees at 0.5). angle_degrees stays as the dihedral source's own threshold. Node is now desktopOnly; catalog regenerated (109 nodes).

cross_field and quad_layout discover feature edges automatically when feature_edges is not wired; public boolean discoverFeatureEdges (default true) on NDirectionField and QuadLayoutEngine disables it and restores the pre-CRAW-5 dihedral fallback byte-for-byte. No system properties.

Unit tests (no mesh files): new sine_ridge.dsl fixture (64x32 grid, y = 0.35 sin(pi x / 2), no crease anywhere) -> discovery traces exactly 4 polylines of 31 points and every discovered edge lies at distance 0.0000 from the analytic lines x = -3, -1, 1, 3; beveled cube through cross_field with NO wiring -> 144 alignment edges covering all 12 bevel bands; tensor-shared-once test (integrateCalls unchanged, sampleReuseCount 1). The pass-1 FeatureEdgeAlignmentTest still green (its fixture now passes use_curvature=false so it still measures the pure dihedral selection).

Benchmark ixdar-app/test/benchmark/FeatureDiscoveryBenchmark.java. Fertility: 1415 feature edges (1446 crest + 158 dihedral before the chain filter), 393 polylines (152 ridge / 241 valley), lengths 2/3/60, tensor 1.34s + trace 0.041s, 27954 disk walks = one per face, second consumer 0 walks. Rocker arm: 4167 edges (4372 + 184), 983 polylines, lengths 2/4/37, tensor 3.76s + trace 0.051s, 70318 walks, second consumer 0 walks. DoD 10 met.

Screenshots (worktree tmp/): craw-5-fertility-discovered-features.png and craw-5-rockerarm-discovered-features.png show the discovered lines with the cross glyphs hidden (key X) following the pedestal rim, limb junctions, bore rims and flange edges with zero DSL wiring; craw-5-fertility-field-and-features.png and craw-5-beveled-cube-aligned-field.png show them under the aligned field. Note --mesh is ignored by cross-field-exam; use --property ixdar.model=<name>.

Fertility baseline reproduced exactly with discovery disabled: 13853 quads, 284 patches, 44 singularities, euler -6. WITH discovery enabled (the default) the field moves to 56 singularities and the run dies in LayoutEmbedding.assertSubcomplex ('10 copy elements are claimed by two T-mesh elements at once') after an OPTIMAL quantization; raising the minimum chain length to 4 (1415 -> 1026 edges) only changes 10 claims to 5. This needs a ruling: fix the embedding, default discoverFeatureEdges to false for quad_layout only, or accept a red fertility layout until the embedding is fixed.

Build and checkstyle green; full unit suite 162 tests with only the known-failing DenseMeshFewSplitsTest ('9 to 37', REFACTOR-PLAN-2 A7) and 1 skipped. Web build green under JDK 25: classes.js 6,753,589 bytes; select_feature_edges is desktopOnly so the quad-layout firewall holds. launch.json gained 'CRAW-5: Cross Field (fertility, auto-discovered features)' (-Dixdar.model=fertility, no feature wiring) alongside the pass-1 beveled-cube entry.

STILL OPEN: (a) the fertility layout crash above; (b) DoD 2's 2-degree bound holds at 0.475 deg on the 96 cone-regular creases but is 3.849 deg on the 48 touching a crease junction, the irreducible 3.75 deg cone bound from pass 1 (awaiting the user's ruling, not chased); (c) the crest lines fragment on scans (median polyline 3-4 vertices, max 60/37) - PATCH-11 territory; (d) the radius/contrast choice is a stand-in for PATCH-100's windowed validity; (e) on the coarse beveled cube the curvature source alone reaches only 4-8 of the 12 bands, the dihedral source carries that model.
